## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two issues should be fixed: `slugify` removes accented and other non-ASCII letters, so it produces mangled or empty slugs, and the PR description is missing the `## Testing` section that `AGENTS.md` requires.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/slug.py` with a regex-based `slugify(title)` helper for building page URLs from titles. It also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py` covering ASCII, repeated hyphens and empty input.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters when building slugs — A title such as `"Café Menu"` becomes `"caf-menu"`, and `"日本語"` becomes `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The PR body says only "non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced, but Python counts `é` and CJK characters as alphanumeric. — Pages with non-English titles get wrong URLs or empty slugs, and different titles can end up with the same URL. — Fix: Either transliterate first (for example `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks) or match with `[\W_]+` under `re.UNICODE`, then add non-ASCII cases to `test_slugify`.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the PR description — The description has no `## Testing` section, which breaks the rule at `AGENTS.md:4`: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Maintainers have no record of how the change was checked, as the project's contributor rules require.
